open_points.subject: INV-020 verification
open_points.text: “a focused test at `import_snapshot` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing” does not say how the test demonstrates that accepted snapshots are never overwritten or deleted, because overwrite or deletion need not be an import input.
open_points.question: Which histories and mutation or persistence surfaces must the INV-020 test exercise to prove append-only retention and immutability?
options: Test only duplicate and conflicting calls to `import_snapshot`.
Also verify that every later operation and persistence surface cannot update or delete an accepted snapshot.
open_points.default_guess: Verify duplicate/conflict imports and inspect or exercise every persistence surface for absence of snapshot update and deletion.

witness.initial: Snapshot version S1 has been accepted and stored.
events: A staff actor performs a later budget operation through a path not exercised by the focused `import_snapshot` test.
That path overwrites or deletes S1.
outcomes: The required focused import test still passes although S1 has disappeared or changed.
A broader invariant test fails because the later path can mutate or delete S1.
witness.observer: A staff or viewer reading snapshot history

open_points.subject: INV-022 verification
open_points.text: “a focused test at `activate_budget_version` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing” does not state how to show both that a producer holds no activation capability and that no activation path can activate its import.
open_points.question: Must INV-022 verify the static producer capability set, rejection by every activation entry point, or only one call to `activate_budget_version`?
options: Exercise one producer call to `activate_budget_version`.
Verify the capability catalog and every activation entry point as well as unchanged state after refusal.
open_points.default_guess: Verify the producer capability catalog and refusal with no writes at every activation entry point.

open_points.subject: INV-023 verification
open_points.text: INV-023 says activation “atomically deactivates the previous active version,” while its Required test only says “a violating input is refused and changes nothing.” It does not describe the normal two-version history that must succeed or what demonstrates atomicity.
open_points.question: What must the test assert when one version is active and another is activated, and what failure injection must show that activation and deactivation are atomic?
options: Treat the presence of an active version as a conflicting input and test refusal.
Activate the new version, assert the old one is deactivated in the same commit, and assert rollback leaves the old state intact on failure.
open_points.default_guess: Test successful replacement plus rollback under a failure between the two state changes.

open_points.subject: INV-024 verification
open_points.text: “a focused test at `upsert_manual_section_plan` showing the invariant holds” does not say how that one test proves all three clauses: at most one manual BudgetVersion, manual-plan mutability only for an active project, and immutability of imported plans.
open_points.question: Which operations and cases must the INV-024 Required test cover for each clause of the invariant?
options: Test only manual-plan upsert behavior.
Also test manual-version creation uniqueness, inactive or archived project refusal, and every surface that could change an imported plan.
open_points.default_guess: Give each clause an explicit case and verify refusal leaves all records unchanged.

open_points.subject: INV-025 verification
open_points.text: The invariant requires automatic linking by `source_key` equality only and forbids display-name matching, but the Required test says “a violating input is refused and changes nothing.” An incoming section with a different key but the same display name is not forbidden input; the linking rules say it is unmatched rather than name-linked.
open_points.question: For different source keys with equal display names, must `_link_snapshot_sections` create or retain distinct section identities, or refuse the whole input?
options: Accept the input and keep or create distinct sections because the keys differ.
Refuse the input and change nothing because the display names collide.
open_points.default_guess: Accept it, assert no name-based link occurs, and keep distinct section identities.

witness.initial: A project has PortalSection A with `source_key=A` and display name “Kitchen”.
events: A later snapshot contains source section B with `source_key=B` and display name “Kitchen”.
The linking function processes the snapshot.
outcomes: B is unmatched and receives a distinct PortalSection identity.
The snapshot or linking operation is refused as a “violating input” and changes nothing.
witness.observer: The operator mapping allocations and the client reading the resulting sections

open_points.subject: source-supplied timestamp inputs
open_points.text: Source times are “the same instant, stored offset-naive UTC,” but “their accepted forms and checks” are merely carried to States 6–7 and are not stated. The texts do not say whether a naive supplied datetime is rejected, interpreted as UTC, or interpreted in some other zone.
open_points.question: Which input datetime forms are accepted for source-supplied instants, and how is each accepted form normalized to offset-naive UTC?
options: Accept only offset-aware datetimes and convert their instant to naive UTC.
Accept naive datetimes and interpret them as UTC.
Accept naive datetimes using a source or local timezone rule.
open_points.default_guess: Accept aware datetimes, normalize to UTC and remove the offset for storage; reject naive inputs.

witness.initial: No record exists for a new snapshot publication.
events: A producer supplies `approved_at` as the naive datetime `2026-10-25 02:30:00` during a timezone transition.
outcomes: The portal accepts it as 02:30 UTC and stores that naive UTC value.
The portal rejects it because no offset identifies an instant.
witness.observer: The producer and later readers of snapshot provenance

open_points.subject: current-time comparisons without timestamp writes
open_points.text: The normative rule covers “every current-time comparison,” but CLK-001 and its Required test are scoped to “an operation that writes timestamps.” No invariant test is specified for operations that compare expiry or validity without writing a timestamp.
open_points.question: What test demonstrates that read-only authentication, authorization, or validity checks obtain exactly one wall reading from the clock source and never read a host clock directly?
options: CLK-001 applies only to operations that write timestamps.
CLK-001 or another invariant also covers every comparison-only operation.
open_points.default_guess: Extend verification to every operation that performs a current-time comparison, whether or not it writes a timestamp.

witness.initial: A staff session expires at instant T.
events: A request resolving that session begins near T and writes no timestamp.
The resolver performs its validity comparison.
outcomes: It uses one injected wall reading and gives a deterministic answer for that operation.
It reads the host clock directly or more than once and can cross T during the check.
witness.observer: The staff caller whose request is accepted or refused

open_points.subject: elapsed clock policy
open_points.text: The new rules require one elapsed-clock reading per request, only through the clock source, as a nondecreasing float used only for the A25 viewer-entry window, but CLK-001 and its Required test mention only wall readings and timestamp-writing operations.
open_points.question: Which formal invariant and Required test verify the elapsed-clock source, reading count, representation, permitted use, and prohibition on storage or conversion to an instant?
options: Treat the elapsed-clock paragraph as untested prose.
Add elapsed-clock obligations to CLK-001.
Define a separate elapsed-clock invariant and test.
open_points.default_guess: Define a separate elapsed-clock invariant with a viewer-entry request test using a fixed monotonic source.

witness.initial: A viewer-entry request arrives at a rate-limit window boundary.
events: The transport guard evaluates the A25 rate limit.
One implementation requests one elapsed value from the shared source; another reads `time.monotonic()` directly or reads it twice.
outcomes: The request is classified using one deterministic elapsed reading.
The request can fall on the other side of the boundary and the shared source cannot verify the reading count.

open_points.subject: DEP-002 age thresholds
open_points.text: `max_snapshot_age` and `max_environment_age` are called “deployment procedure values,” but no values or rule for selecting them is given. They determine whether a deploy starts and therefore leave exact refusal conditions open.
open_points.question: What are the maximum snapshot and environment ages, in what units, and from which configured authority does the deploy route obtain them?
options: Fixed values defined by the Factory deploy route.
Per-environment configured values with specified validation.
Unbounded or implementation-selected values.
open_points.default_guess: Require explicit positive duration values from the deploy route and fail closed when either is absent or invalid.

witness.initial: An image has a passing vulnerability verdict based on an OSV snapshot that is 25 hours old.
events: The deployment route attempts to start the image.
outcomes: The deploy is refused because the configured maximum is 24 hours.
The deploy starts because the configured maximum is 48 hours.
witness.observer: The deployment operator and service users

open_points.subject: maximum environment age
open_points.text: The Required test introduces a verdict “no older than its maximum environment age,” but rule 3 and DEP-002 define only the OSV snapshot age and do not define “environment age,” its starting instant, or what event refreshes it.
open_points.question: What object is aged by `max_environment_age`, when does its age begin, and must restarting the same unchanged image obtain a new verdict after that age?
options: Age the vulnerability verdict from completion of the scan.
Age the built image from its creation time.
Age the installed distribution inventory from resolution or installation.
Apply the limit only to a first start, not later restarts.
open_points.default_guess: Measure from completion of the verdict bound to the image content and require a fresh passing verdict for every deploy after expiry.

witness.initial: A built image passed its release gate two hours ago and has not changed.
events: The route attempts to start the same image again.
outcomes: The restart is refused because the image-bound verdict exceeded `max_environment_age`.
The restart is allowed because the image is unchanged or because environment age starts at restart.

open_points.subject: image identity binding
open_points.text: The Required test binds the verdict to the image's “content id” and refuses “another image,” but neither the normative rule nor the invariant defines which image identifier or content boundary establishes sameness.
open_points.question: Which immutable identifier proves that the scanned image and the started image are the same, including platform-specific variants and image metadata?
options: OCI manifest digest.
Image configuration digest.
A deployment-system-generated content hash over a specified image closure.
A mutable image tag.
open_points.default_guess: Use the immutable OCI manifest digest for the exact platform image and reject tags or mismatched digests.

witness.initial: Image tag `portal:release` pointed to digest D1 when the vulnerability check passed.
events: The tag is moved to digest D2.
outcomes: The start is refused because D2 differs from the checked immutable content identifier.
The start proceeds because the tag string is treated as the content id.
witness.observer: The deployment operator and users of the started service
